fields.h1: Build a Food Bank Application Form That Knows Each Household
fields.hero_description: Get a food bank application form that sizes each grocery box and keeps the household on file for the next visit.
fields.features_heading: What a Paper Intake Sheet Leaves to Volunteers
fields.features_subheading: A paper sheet records a family once. These six pieces carry that record from the first visit to every one after it.
fields.feature_1:
Household size, counted by age

The form asks how many adults, children, and seniors live in the home and adds them up. Volunteers packing groceries see the total, so a family of 6 never gets a box for 2.
fields.feature_2:
A saved record for every return visit

A volunteer finds a returning household by phone number and sees what was entered last time. The client only answers what has changed, such as a new baby or a new address.
fields.feature_3:
One question per screen on a phone

Clients can fill out the form on their own phone while they wait in line, one short question at a time. Nobody has to read their answers out loud at the intake table.
fields.feature_4:
Dietary needs that reach the packing table

Ask once about allergies and any foods a family does not eat. Each need appears beside the box size on the packing screen at every visit, not only the first time they come in.
fields.feature_5:
Client records in a database you own

Every family's record is saved to a database your food bank owns, with no cap on responses. Pull a list for a partner agency or a count for a funder without retyping a thing.
fields.feature_6:
The code, exported to your GitHub

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository. A volunteer developer can host it next to your other tools or connect it to systems your network uses.

fields.usecase_heading: Food Bank Intake at Four Pantry Doors
fields.tab_content_1:
One gluten-free swap in a box for 5

Odalys Brenner walks into Larkspur Hollow Pantry for the first time with a household of 2 adults and 3 children. She fills out the form on her phone while in line and notes that her youngest eats gluten-free. At the packing table, the volunteer's screen shows a box for 5 with 1 gluten-free swap.
fields.tab_content_2:
Wendell checks in with one tap

Wendell Ashgrove has picked up groceries at Fernhill Community Pantry before. A volunteer looks him up by phone number, and the form shows his household of 4 from his September 12 visit. Nothing has changed since then. He taps No changes, and his check-in is saved.
fields.tab_content_3:
From one request to stop 14 on Tuesday

Sunmeadow Food Bank drives groceries on Tuesdays to clients who cannot get to a pantry. Tobiah Marsh stopped driving this year and picks home delivery on the form. Coordinator Ines Halloway gets an email with his address and his household of 1, and he becomes stop 14 on the Tuesday route.
fields.tab_content_4:
All of October, counted by age: 1,268 people

Renata Oyelaran opens October on the Coldbrook Valley Food Bank dashboard before the board meets. The month shows 412 households. Because every family listed its members by age at intake, the people served add up on their own: 702 adults, 418 children, and 148 seniors, for 1,268 in all.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Food Bank Application Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a food bank application form that sizes each box and keeps every household ready for its next visit.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down what your pantry uses
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask about food, not about people
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down what your pantry actually uses at the table, such as family size and how a client gets groceries home. If nobody acts on an answer, leave the question off and keep the line moving.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for the number of adults, children, and seniors as three separate counts instead of one total. The box size and your monthly report both draw on those counts, and families answer them in seconds.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask which foods the family cannot eat or chooses not to eat, with a short list and an Other box. Keep the wording plain and kind, and never ask a client to explain why.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide how a returning household is found, such as by phone number, and what they confirm each time. With a short check-in screen, volunteers never hand the full form to a family every month.
fields.howto_step_5_des: If you deliver, offer delivery next to pickup and name the coordinator who plans the route. Give the coordinator the address and the number of people with each request, and nothing they do not use.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Put your questions and the delivery routing into one prompt. Emergent builds the food bank application form, the database behind it, and a dashboard. Change anything later with a new prompt.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Have a volunteer take one real visit through intake and on to the packing screen. Check that the box size and the dietary note are right, then try a return check-in with the same phone number.

faq_plan.q: What is a food bank application form?
faq_plan.a: A food bank application form is the intake a household fills out to get groceries from a food bank or one of its pantries. It records how many people the groceries are for and how to reach them, along with any dietary needs. The pantry uses those answers to size each box and to count the people it serves.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a food bank application form?
faq_plan.a: Decide what your pantry needs from each client, such as head counts by age and a pickup or delivery choice. Describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. Emergent builds the form and the database behind it, and each household you register is saved there for the next visit.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a food bank application form include?
faq_plan.a: Start with a name and a phone number, then a count of the people at home in each age group. Add dietary needs, a preferred language, and whether the client will pick up or needs delivery. Leave off any question your pantry does not act on.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a food bank application form have?
faq_plan.a: Keep it to 12 questions or fewer, short enough to finish on a phone while waiting in line. Skip the employment history and landlord details a rental application form asks for. If a program you run needs more, add those questions on a second screen that only the households in that program see.

faq_plan.q: Should a food bank application form be online or on paper?
faq_plan.a: Online, for a busy pantry, with a few paper copies on hand. A food bank application form PDF has to be printed, filled in by hand, and typed up later by someone who can read the handwriting. An online form saves each household as it is submitted, and clients can fill it out on their own phone.

faq_plan.q: How do you keep answers on a food bank application form private?
faq_plan.a: Collect only what you use, and let only the staff and volunteers who need the records open them. Have clients answer sensitive questions on their own phone instead of out loud at the table. With Emergent, client records live in a database you own instead of a shared spreadsheet.

faq_plan.q: What should a food bank application form leave out?
faq_plan.a: Leave out Social Security numbers, bank details, and employer names unless a program you run asks for them. Questions like those belong on a credit application form, not on intake for groceries. Every question you drop makes the form easier for someone asking for help for the first time.

faq_plan.q: How often should a household update its food bank application form?
faq_plan.a: Have returning clients confirm their details at every visit, and ask for a full update once a year or whenever the household changes. Watch for a new baby or a relative moving in, because either one changes the box size. A check-in screen found by phone number keeps that confirmation to one tap.

faq_plan.q: Can a volunteer fill out a food bank application form for a client?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A volunteer can enter the answers on a tablet while the client talks, which helps anyone without a phone or who prefers not to type. Mark which entries a volunteer filled in so you know who to follow up with. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps, however long the line gets.

faq_plan.q: Can a food bank application form take home delivery requests?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Offer delivery as an answer next to pickup, and route each delivery request to one coordinator along with the address. Volunteer drivers are a separate group: sign them up through a driver application form and keep their details apart from client records.

plan.angle: The top 10 is seven food banks' own paper or PDF assistance applications, a county pantry page, a Scribd blank and one Jotform template: each records a household once and stops. None counts the household by age for packing, pulls a returning client's saved details at the next visit, routes a home delivery request to the person who plans the route, or totals the month for the board. This page is for food banks and pantries building their own client intake, with those four jobs, in respectful plain wording and with no eligibility rules.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Food Bank Application Form That Knows Each Household'; hero 'Get a food bank application form that sizes each grocery box and keeps the household on file for the next visit.' covers the whole intake job, not one feature.

intent.evidence: AMBER angle carried: pantries building client intake ('What a Paper Intake Sheet Leaves to Volunteers'); how-to, FAQ on questions to include and what to leave out, and the PDF secondary in why_intro and FAQ 5. No eligibility rules, no income or benefit claims.

specificity.evidence: Pantry vocabulary throughout: 'packing table', 'box for 5 with 1 gluten-free swap', 'stop 14 on the Tuesday route', '702 adults, 418 children, and 148 seniors'.

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: 'The form asks how many adults, children, and seniors live in the home', 'Odalys Brenner walks into Larkspur Hollow Pantry'.

craft.evidence: One ', so' ending ('see the total, so a family of 6 never gets a box for 2'), under the cap; sentences short and varied.

voice.evidence: Plain, respectful wording: 'Keep the wording plain and kind, and never ask a client to explain why.' No hype vocabulary.

truth.evidence: FAQ 5 'A food bank application form PDF has to be printed, filled in by hand' and why_intro 'A food bank application form PDF gets typed up after the line clears' state as a universal fact what is false for fillable PDFs; no domain source. Emergent claims map to prompt-build, database-owned, alerts, conversational, no-caps, code-export; tab 4 numbers add up (702+418+148=1,268; 96+104+99+113=412).

distinct.evidence: Reads as client intake for a pantry (household counts by age, return check-in, delivery routing, board totals); nothing shared with food-order, catering-order or donation pages; QC D2 clean.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic intake questions ('What should a food bank application form leave out?', 'Can a volunteer fill out a food bank application form for a client?'), each answered first; hub link in item 2; no brand or file-format asks.

images.evidence: Contact sheet (2026-10-26) matches tab copy: 'Box for 5', '1 gluten-free swap', 'Household of 4', 'Same as his September 12 visit', 'Email to Ines Halloway', 'Tuesday route, stop 14', weeks 96/104/99/113 summing to 412, '1,268 people served'. One hero per panel.
